claim.pdf_says: 13.18.38.2 General formats, 'Format 3 (report-writer):' is printed as a general-format figure in the diagram font with four words UNDERLINED: 'OCCURS [ integer-1 TO ] integer-2 TIMES [ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ] [ STEP integer-3 ]' - OCCURS, TO, DEPENDING and STEP each carry an underline rule; TIMES, ON, integer-1, integer-2, integer-3 and data-name-1 do not.
claim.markdown_says: Line 41 of the page-460 slice: 'OCCURS [ integer-1 TO ] integer-2 TIMES [ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ] [ STEP integer-3 ]' - transcribed as an ordinary markdown paragraph, outside any fenced block, with NO accompanying 'Figure notes' paragraph. Formats 1, 2 and 4 on the same page are each fenced and each carry a figure-notes paragraph recording their underlining; Format 3 alone records none.
claim.why_it_matters: This transcription carries the required-word (underline) information in the figure-notes paragraphs, because plain-text code fences cannot show underlining. For Format 3 that information is simply absent, so the markdown no longer records that OCCURS, TO, DEPENDING and STEP are required words while TIMES and ON are optional words. Rendering the format as prose rather than a fenced figure also loses its identity as a general format for any tool that walks the fenced blocks.

verdict.reasoning: PDF side CONFIRMED by rendering page 460 at 300 dpi and zooming the Format 3 line (crop y=1890..2000 of E:/Temp/specrecon/v460/spec_p460.png, saved as fmt3_zoom.png). I read the printed glyphs directly: an underline rule sits under OCCURS, under TO, under DEPENDING, and under STEP. There is no rule under TIMES, ON, integer-1, integer-2, integer-3 or data-name-1. Exactly the four words the claim names, and no others. Markdown side CONFIRMED: the workunit slice line 41 corresponds to specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 19557, which is byte-for-byte 'OCCURS [ integer-1 TO ] integer-2 TIMES [ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ] [ STEP integer-3 ]' - unfenced, and carrying none of the three mechanisms this file uses elsewhere to record underlining: no <u>...</u> tags (cf. lines 12927, 14782, 18303, 20765), no LaTeX \underline{} (cf. lines 25254, 27037), and no 'Figure notes' paragraph. The underline record is therefore genuinely absent, and the absence is load-bearing content, not typography: the standard's own conventions clause (transcribed at md lines 2628, 5770 and 5805) makes underlining normative - uppercase underlined = keyword, required; uppercase not underlined = optional word, 'may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics'. Concretely, nothing in the markdown records that STEP must be written whenever the bracketed STEP phrase is used; I grepped every STEP occurrence (md lines 10763, 16705, 19557, 19665, 19678, 19786, 19796, 47002+) and its required-word status is recorded nowhere, including the parallel plain transcription of the same phrase inside the report-group-entry composite format at line 16705. So the finding is real. Two parts of the claim's framing are wrong, however, and I refute them. (1) 'Formats 1, 2 and 4 on the same page are each fenced' is false: Format 4's first line (md line 19561, 'OCCURS DYNAMIC [ CAPACITY IN data-name-3 ] [FROM integer-4 ] [ TO integer-5 ] [ INITIALIZED ]') is unfenced prose exactly like Format 3; only its ASCENDING/DESCENDING continuation is fenced. What actually distinguishes Format 4 is that its figure-notes paragraph explicitly records the unfenced line's underlining ('OCCURS, DYNAMIC, CAPACITY, FROM, TO, and INITIALIZED are underlined; IN is not'). The defect is the missing notes paragraph, not the missing fence. (2) 'Rendering the format as prose rather than a fenced figure loses its identity as a general format' overstates a document-wide style choice into a page-460 defect: I surveyed all 166 'Format N (...)' headings in the file and 63 of them are followed by unfenced text, so single-line formats as prose is this transcription's normal convention, and no fenced-block-walking tool could ever have relied on the fence. Also note the bracket structure - the actual optionality of [ integer-1 TO ], [ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ] and [ STEP integer-3 ] - IS transcribed correctly and completely; the loss is confined to the required-word underlining. Mitigating but not exculpating: the identical words OCCURS/TO/DEPENDING/TIMES/ON have their underline status stated one figure earlier in the Format 2 notes (md line 19553), so a careful human reader could infer all of Format 3's underlining except STEP's from the same page. STEP is the one datum with no record anywhere.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with the framing corrected. Page 460, 13.18.38.2, Format 3 (report-writer): the PDF prints 'OCCURS [ integer-1 TO ] integer-2 TIMES [ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ] [ STEP integer-3 ]' with underline rules under OCCURS, TO, DEPENDING and STEP only (verified glyph-by-glyph in a 300-dpi zoom). The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 19557 = page-460 slice line 41) reproduces the text and its bracket structure exactly, but records the underlining by none of the file's three available mechanisms - no <u> tags, no \underline{}, and no 'Figure notes' paragraph - so the required-vs-optional-word distinction that the standard's own conventions clause makes normative (md lines 2628/5770/5805) is lost for this figure. The one datum recorded nowhere in the whole file is that STEP is a required word: STEP's underline means the keyword must be written whenever the bracketed phrase is used. Two claim details are wrong: Format 4's opening line is ALSO unfenced prose (md line 19561), so the page does not contrast 'fenced formats vs prose Format 3' - it contrasts formats that have a figure-notes paragraph recording their underlining against Format 3, which has none; and unfenced single-line general formats are this transcription's standard style (63 of 166 'Format N' headings), so the missing fence is not itself a defect and no tool contract is broken by it. Fix: add the underline record, either as inline markup - '<u>OCCURS</u> [ integer-1 <u>TO</u> ] integer-2 TIMES [ <u>DEPENDING</u> ON data-name-1 ] [ <u>STEP</u> integer-3 ]' - or as a Format 3 figure-notes paragraph naming OCCURS, TO, DEPENDING, STEP as underlined and TIMES, ON as not. Severity is better characterized as content-loss/minor than structural: one figure's required-word annotation, not a structural corruption. Separate whitespace nit spotted while checking, not part of this claim: the Format 4 line transcribes '[FROM integer-4 ]' where the PDF prints '[ FROM integer-4 ]'.
